hypothesis: Increasing the CTA from 8 to 32 target warps may reduce scheduling overhead while preserving the warp-per-target traversal. The larger CTA could also reduce occupancy, so its effect must be measured after correctness passes.
notes: Configuration-only experiment: the existing kernel already handles source and target tails, excludes self pairs, softens coincident positions, and writes the complete output state from one lane per target. This candidate has not been tested; correctness-gate it before measuring. Supplied observations report 0.1530 s for the 8-warp parent and 0.1174 s for a prior 16-warp candidate, but do not establish how 32 warps will perform.
transformations: Set block to 1024 threads (32 warps) and items_per_block to 32, maintaining the required block/32 mapping.
Kept shared_memory_bytes at 0 and left the source kernel unchanged.
